subject: Automotive & EVs
title: André Citroën's Bold Bets
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: André Citroën's Bold Bets.

hook.text: André Citroën was the French Henry Ford—a showman who turned car-making into mass entertainment.

buildup.text: He plastered his name on the Eiffel Tower in lights and drove cars across the Sahara for publicity.

discovery.text: His 1934 Traction Avant was the first mass-produced front-wheel-drive car—decades ahead of its time.

twist.text: His bold spending bankrupted the company. Michelin took over and Citroën lost his own brand.

climax.text: He died in 1935, but his engineering DNA still lives in every front-wheel-drive car today.

punchline.text: Citroën bet everything on the future—and went broke proving it.

quiz.question: What was pioneering about the Citroën Traction Avant?

details.summary: Andre Citroen was a visionary French industrialist who introduced mass production to Europe, pioneered front-wheel drive, and used daring marketing stunts that made his brand synonymous with innovation.
details.whyItMatters: Citroen proved that European automakers could compete with Ford's mass-production model while pushing design and engineering boundaries that shaped the French automotive industry for decades.
takeaways: Citroen brought assembly line production to France in the 1920s
He organized Sahara and Asia expeditions to promote his brand
Financial overreach on innovation ultimately bankrupted him

faq.question: What made Citroen different from other early automakers?
faq.answer: Citroen combined industrial efficiency with bold marketing and avant-garde design. He was the first to light up the Eiffel Tower with his name and organized transcontinental expeditions as publicity stunts.

faq.question: Why did Andre Citroen go bankrupt?
faq.answer: He invested heavily in the revolutionary Traction Avant, the first mass-produced front-wheel drive car. The cost of retooling his factory exceeded the company's finances, and he lost control to Michelin in 1934.
